prompt: An unmarked ship offers cheap labor and a suspiciously large crate of spare parts. Their crew keeps asking where we store the oxygen.

random_outcomes.text: They were pirates. They left a handwritten invoice for the oxygen they stole.

prompt: An alien casino has opened in the colony. The house accepts lunar crystals and claims its dice are legally sentient.

random_outcomes.text: The dice unionized mid-game and seized the table. Your winnings are now a labor dispute.

prompt: A new supplement promises better focus during long shifts. The label lists moon dust, vitamins, and one ingredient marked simply: probably fine.

random_outcomes.text: Half the volunteers laugh continuously. The other half publish a very cheerful incident report.

prompt: A hydroponics rig can grow leafy greens twice as fast, but it wants a third of our clean water and a technician who keeps calling lettuce a colleague.

random_outcomes.text: The nutrient pump floods one bay. The lettuce survives and requests a transfer.

prompt: Bob wants to raise two miniature goats for milk. They have already eaten the emergency crop schedule and one corner of the colony charter.

random_outcomes.text: A goat escapes into the greenhouse and eats three months of salad in eleven minutes.

prompt: A drill team found a clean ice seam beneath the ridge. The sample is promising; the map was drawn on a napkin during a rover race.

random_outcomes.text: The drill reaches ice, then a pocket of abrasive dust. The water is excellent; the machinery is not.

prompt: Earth can send a supply pallet next month. It costs a fortune, and the manifest lists three crates as assorted mystery cables.

random_outcomes.text: A customs delay swaps our water filters for commemorative flags. The flags are very nice.

prompt: A government grant will cover a new habitat wing if we promise weekly progress calls and one tasteful plaque per square meter.

random_outcomes.text: The plaque contractor invoices us for the wall behind the plaque. A committee is reviewing the wall.

prompt: The aliens offer a direct translation channel. Their first message is either a generous trade proposal or a very detailed complaint about our Moon naming conventions.

random_outcomes.text: The translator mistakes a greeting for a binding purchase of twelve ceremonial spoons.

prompt: A sensor spotted movement near the perimeter. Security wants a costly upgrade; the sensor's manual says it can also detect determined squirrels.
There is room to expand the habitat. The new wing adds beds and privacy, but its current blueprint includes a hallway that ends at a wall.

random_outcomes.text: A support frame buckles. The hallway now ends at a different wall.

prompt: Mars offers food in exchange for repair parts. Their cargo launch window is short, and their pilot has never seen a window that opens outward.

random_outcomes.text: The shipment arrives full of dehydrated birthday cake. Mars says the real food is on the next launch.

prompt: Radiation readings are climbing. We can add shielding around the sleeping quarters or move the crew to a smaller, very noisy storage module.
A solar storm will hit in two days. The shelter plan uses extra supplies; skipping it keeps the power bank full but leaves the greenhouse exposed.

random_outcomes.text: A backup inverter trips during the storm. The crew is safe, and the lights now blink in Morse code.

prompt: The oxygen scrubber is running hot. A replacement is expensive; a repair is cheap and comes with the engineer's assurance that the noise is normal.
The sleeping quarters are crowded. We can convert the gym into bunks or offer a funded return flight to a few volunteers.
Scientists want to study a strange mineral that hums when nobody is looking directly at it. The lab needs supplies and a strict no-humming policy.

random_outcomes.text: The mineral powers a lab lamp for three days, then hums the colony anthem in a new key.

prompt: The maintenance team can modernize the water pumps. The upgrade saves supplies later, but will take a week and one very specific wrench from Earth.
A two-person crew is stranded near our landing zone. Their ship has supplies but its navigation system keeps announcing the wrong planet.

random_outcomes.text: One astronaut is a brilliant mechanic. The other has been narrating every repair like a sports final.

prompt: A senator offers a funding boost in exchange for a guided tour and a promise not to mention the airlock incident on camera.
A corporation will bankroll our next shipment for exclusive rights to every discovery. Their contract defines discovery to include new sandwich combinations.

random_outcomes.text: The sponsor claims ownership of the colony's algae recipe. The recipe is mostly water and a secret.

prompt: A smuggler offers black-market batteries at half price. He says they're new, though every battery is stamped with a different year.

random_outcomes.text: One battery starts playing a message from a ship that has not launched yet.

prompt: An alien trader offers rare filter mesh for water and a modest fee. They insist our currency is “delightfully flat.”

random_outcomes.text: The mesh is excellent. The trader also leaves with our entire collection of novelty coins.

prompt: A recovered alien device could improve power storage. It is warm, softly glowing, and labeled in a language that may be warning us about fingerprints.

random_outcomes.text: The device charges a battery bank, then politely refuses to work for anyone wearing shoes.

prompt: A buried lunar artifact is sending a signal from beneath the oldest crater. The aliens ask us not to dig; the archaeologist asks us not to tell the aliens.

random_outcomes.text: The artifact opens and projects a map. It is upside down and includes our cafeteria.

prompt: A regional dust front is heading toward the colony. The forecast is clear about the dust and vague about the part called “sideways.”
A batch of maintenance robots can take over night repairs. They are efficient, but have formed a book club that only reads warning labels.

random_outcomes.text: The robots repair the pump and alphabetize every label in the habitat. Nobody can find the emergency exit instructions.

prompt: A hidden market sells medical supplies and suspiciously fresh coffee. The dealer accepts credits, favors, or one very good secret.

random_outcomes.text: The kit is real. The coffee is a tiny alien plant that has started following the medic.

prompt: The crew wants a zero-gravity movie night. The projector works, but the only film file is a six-hour documentary about printer maintenance.
The night shift wants safer hours and a real day off. The current schedule has a day off listed as “Tuesday, if Tuesday happens.”
It is time for a colony election. The two leading candidates are a botanist and a ballot box with suspiciously strong polling numbers.

random_outcomes.text: The ballot box wins by a landslide. It promises to reduce paperwork by eliminating paper.

prompt: Kestrel's air recycler is failing. They want our spare filters now and promise to repay us after their next shipment. Their next shipment has been next week for six months.

random_outcomes.text: Kestrel repays us in rare ice. Their accountant also sends a handwritten apology.

prompt: Earth wants to send the first luxury tour group. Guests expect low gravity, high luxury, and a quick selfie outside the habitat.

random_outcomes.text: A guest livestreams the airlock code. The clip gets twelve million views before security spots it.

prompt: Several groups want the same crater for a reflection garden. Their opening ceremony requires one shared loudspeaker and six incompatible playlists.

no.text: Keep the crater a science site

prompt: The medical AI diagnoses everyone with insufficient moon. Its old version thinks bandages are a food group; its new version has started billing the patients.
Helix offers a large advance for exclusive rights to a polar ice deposit. Their contract defines exclusive as until a lawyer gets bored.

random_outcomes.text: The deposit is sacred to nearby aliens. Helix's survey drone is returned in several pieces.

no.text: Keep the ice in public hands

prompt: A solar-sail test could make future cargo runs cheaper. The prototype is stadium-sized and currently tied to a very nervous delivery tug.

random_outcomes.text: The sail catches sunlight perfectly. Earth agrees to cover part of next month's freight bill.

prompt: A moonquake swarm rattles the south habitat. Engineers can reinforce the supports, or evacuate and hope the next tremor lands somewhere less embarrassing.

random_outcomes.text: The final brace reveals a cracked coolant pipe. The repair crew calls the timing technically helpful.

prompt: A cloud of old satellite panels crosses our landing corridor. A tug can clear the path, but it burns fuel reserved for the next cargo window.
The kids outgrew the storage-closet school. Their plan is orbital mechanics, lunar gardening, and a formal petition to remove algebra.

random_outcomes.text: The students grow edible algae for the cafeteria. The algebra petition remains under review.

prompt: A network offers a live reality-show deal. They want dramatic music and veto power over scenes where people calmly maintain equipment.
Earth recalls eight specialists to help with a crisis back home. Their replacements arrive in four months, assuming the transfer paperwork gets its own transfer paperwork.
The aliens offer a living garden that filters air and water. It only grows under their music, which sounds like a kettle discovering jazz.

random_outcomes.text: The garden blooms, then serenades the night shift at a volume usually reserved for launch alarms.

prompt: Artists want to paint a mural across the habitat's radiation shield. Their beautiful draft currently covers the access-hatch label.
Colonists want a binding charter before the next election. The draft guarantees every resident a vote and gives the commander emergency authority unless it is inconvenient.
A new cough spreads through the sleeping quarters. Quarantine disrupts two shifts; skipping it keeps the oxygen plant staffed today.
The maintenance crew wants repair bots treated as coworkers, not equipment. The bots counterpropose better charging outlets.
A sponsor funds new water tanks if each is painted with their mascot: a straw wearing sunglasses. The tanks are very large.

yes.text: Put the straw on the tanks

random_outcomes.text: The aliens interpret the mascot as a declaration of war against beverages. Negotiations get unusually specific.

prompt: A long eclipse cuts solar power for three days. We can ration now or keep normal meals and hope the backup batteries outlast the optimism briefing.
Colonists want to race utility rovers around the landing pad. The safety plan is thorough, except for the section titled what if the Moon is dusty.

random_outcomes.text: A rover kicks up dust that spells the colony name from orbit. Tourism bookings surge; the filters do not.
